verdict.rationale: Unity documents public scripting APIs for finer control and editor extension, command-line and headless automation of the Editor, and a first-party CLI whose `unity <command>`/`unity eval` drive the Editor directly, with an MCP mode for agents. Together these give broad programmatic access to Editor functionality. No evidence states that everything in the UI is available through the API, and no OpenAPI spec exists. missing for 10: an explicit documented UI/API parity guarantee, a coverage map of which Editor actions are exposed programmatically, and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Interacting directly with the public Unity APIs allows for finer control and a greater degree of customization.
`unity <command>`/`unity eval` drive the Editor directly without MCP
